framework.summary: Department rules must require developers to report pre-development plans; the bill itself sets no developer-written safety framework.
framework.quote: Requirements for entities developing artificial intelligence to report pre-development plans to the Department.

transparency_report.summary: The bill requires no public report or disclosure about a model.

incident_reporting.summary: Anyone who discovers a superintelligence, or an AI with superintelligence precursor traits, must notify the Secretary within 24 hours; this covers discoveries, not general safety incidents.
incident_reporting.quote: shall submit to the Secretary notice of the discovery within 24 hours.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The only reporting window is the 24-hour discovery notice; no separate shorter window for imminent risk of death or injury.

third_party_audit.summary: Department rules must include auditing of organizational safety practices; the text does not say an independent third party audits.
third_party_audit.quote: Auditing to evaluate and improve organizational safety practices relating to artificial intelligence development.

whistleblower.summary: Employers may not retaliate against employees or contractors, current or former, who give information about a violation of the Act to the Department, law enforcement or Congress.
whistleblower.quote: No employer may, directly or indirectly, discharge, demote, suspend, threaten, blacklist, harass, or in any other manner discriminate against a covered individual

registration.summary: No one may develop or distribute an advanced AI model without a charter from the Secretary, and no advanced system may be deployed without pre-deployment approval.
registration.quote: No person may develop or distribute an advanced artificial intelligence model without a charter issued by the Secretary under subsection (a).

shutdown.summary: The Secretary must pause and sequester any AI showing superintelligence precursor traits, and render it inoperative within 30 days if not cleared; superintelligences are destroyed immediately.
shutdown.quote: is rendered inoperative before the date that is 30 days after the date on which the Secretary makes the identification described in such subsection with respect to such system

compute_threshold.summary: An advanced AI system is one trained on at least 10^25 operations, adjusted each year by the Secretary to keep the same equivalence.
compute_threshold.quote: trained on computing power greater than or equal to 10^25 integer or floating point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: The bill defines coverage by no revenue, spending or user figure.

harm_threshold.summary: The bill defines harm by capability (superintelligence, precursor traits), with no death, injury or damages figure.

penalties.summary: Reckless violators face up to 20 years in prison and fines (title 18); other individuals face 10-year industry bans; the Secretary can revoke charters and force forfeiture, subject to review by the Federal Circuit.
penalties.quote: recklessly violates section 8, 9, or 12 or a rule promulgated thereunder shall be fined under title 18, United States Code, and imprisoned for not more than 20 years.

effective_date.summary: The pause on advanced AI begins on the date of enactment and lasts until the Secretary finds the Department staffed and its rules issued.
effective_date.quote: the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on the date on which the Secretary determines that

notes: Entry names companion H.R. 10538; its text was not read. Bill bans superintelligence and imposes a development pause; most duties are Department rules still to be written (Sec. 8(c)). Effective_date marked partial because the pause starts on enactment but the rest awaits rulemaking.
